headline: LEO constellations rise. Acquisitions abound. Funding flows.
deck: This week saw significant moves in satellite constellations, acquisitions, and funding rounds that highlight the competitive landscape.

stories.head: MDA Space buys Blue Canyon for $620M
stories.body: MDA Space announced its acquisition of Blue Canyon Technologies for $620 million, aiming to bolster its presence in the U.S. market. This move is a strategic play to enhance capabilities in small satellite systems, which are increasingly vital for modern space operations. The deal underscores the trend of established players opting for mergers over organic growth.
stories.soWhat: Sometimes, it’s easier to buy a seat at the table than to build your own.

stories.head: True Anomaly secures $190M Series C
stories.body: True Anomaly raised $190 million in Series C funding, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, reflecting a growing interest in defense applications. This funding round emphasizes that in the space sector, cash often trumps actual innovation.
stories.soWhat: In space, it seems the money is more about the promise than the product.

stories.head: Jio Platforms unveils LEO plans ahead of IPO
stories.body: Jio Platforms is laying out its ambitious plans for a sovereign LEO constellation to lease broadband capacity, coinciding with its upcoming IPO. This move is expected to position Jio as a key player in the satellite broadband market, especially as demand for connectivity continues to rise. It’s a classic case of leveraging an IPO to fund satellite ambitions.
stories.soWhat: Who needs to build satellites when you can just lease the spectrum?

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
